correctness.rationale: Coprime normalization preserves gcd. The Bézout identity gives two complementary nonnegative candidate witnesses with exactly one parity admissible; unimodular inverse transport has correct normalization. Six possible F2 states exhaust the Bézout parity constraint and split into three 2-cycles for even k or two 3-cycles for odd k. Checks: 68,094 modular inverse recalculations, 58,782 period comparisons, 9,269 complete small integer solution enumerations, 2,640 normalized noncoprime cases. Scope and finite verification limits explicit.

value.rationale: The Diophantine midpoint pair and the dependence of solvable equations on recurrence families are published mathematical questions. The arbitrary initial pair and coefficient k>=2 obtain a sharp, contrasting period law plus explicit unique integer coordinates at every index; this extends only restricted balancing cases, distinguishing additive and subtractive companion dynamics. The new theorem solves a natural full recurrence family, not an arbitrary sample or mere computational census.
